external_fixture.contract: Selected v2 GET /pods and GET/PUT /account/ssh-keys through declared proxy prefixes, strict bearer authentication, exact pods/pagination and key-list envelopes, full replacement and problem+json errors. The original account chain retains its exact19-call oracle; added URL, whitespace and key-rotation chains each have independent exact ordered method/path/query/auth/body/response ledgers. Optional raw query is a fixture-owned reverse-proxy identity and must match byte-for-byte. Default HTTPS uses an offline CONNECT/TLS fixture restricted to api.runpod.io:443 with private CA, matching SNI and HTTP/1.1 ALPN; expected GET/PUT counts follow the known existing-key state without resetting it. Unrelated auto-update/usage activity is disabled by real installation controls. No live cloud provisioning or literal optional endpoint omission is claimed.

cleanup: Trace, browser context, browser, server, log copy, report write and artifact scan are guarded independently. PASS is aggregated only after business success and successful teardown/scan. Unresolved provider IDs stay scoped to the isolated private database; an unconfirmed server exit retains its PID/reclaim entry. test_provider_endpoint_cleanup.py drives the actual main through normal success and trace/context/browser/server/log/report/scan/business failures, proves later closes still run and an earlier failure never becomes PASS.

checklist_items.1.1: On first open the RunPod add dialog shows the RunPod type in its only combobox. Name is an empty required textbox without an HTML maxlength; the real API bounds it at 256 Unicode code points. Its placeholder is the localized example that includes RunPod. API endpoint is a textbox whose value and placeholder are https://api.runpod.io/v2. It is not required and has no maximum length. API key is an empty password textbox, required, with no maximum length, placeholder API Key, and one visibility control. There is no spinbutton and there are three textboxes. The create POST sends kind runpod, the typed name, that endpoint, and the API key. The independent GET stores the id, kind runpod, the name, the endpoint, an empty public key, and an empty extra object, and it omits the API key.
checklist_items.1.2: On first open the RunPod dialog shows the RunPod type, an empty name, the endpoint default from the kind catalog, and an empty API key. While the saved-account GET is held, Save stays disabled and the endpoint is still empty, so the incomplete form cannot be submitted. After that GET the saved name and endpoint are backfilled and the API key stays empty.
checklist_items.1.3: Every required text field is asserted to have a correct refusal path. Name is textual and its required rule now declares whitespace:true, so an empty value and a whitespace-only value are both refused in the browser: the nameRequired message appears on that field, the field keeps what was typed, no PUT or POST leaves the browser, the provider is not contacted, the account collection is unchanged, and the stored name is read back as the original. The API key is a credential whose blank value can only be judged by the provider, so its whitespace value is asserted to reach the real server and come back as a 400 with the exact credential refusal reason, with the dialog kept open and the typed value retained. kind is a Select and has no whitespace case. Proven by mutation: dropping whitespace:true from the name rule makes the case fail because the nameRequired message never appears, and the case no longer asserts the old behaviour of a whitespace name being accepted with the saved name retained.
checklist_items.1.4: Within the actual RunPod name/endpoint/API-key form, name boundaries exercise1/255/256 Unicode code points,257 rejection and a browser-preserved prohibited control, with exact FIELD_INVALID error, unchanged GET and no external validation on rejection; empty required names are frontend-refused and whitespace follows create-preserve/edit-trim-or-retain semantics. Optional endpoint boundaries cover empty/whitespace defaults or retention, FTP, hostless URL, invalid ports, repeated prefix, valid port/path/query and correction. Key boundaries cover empty/whitespace/authentication errors and an actual UI-entered NUL rejected before any external request with the exact Authorization-header error; clearing that draft saves successfully and UI Sync still authenticates B. Endpoint/key have no invented field-length maximum. Length/control-name cases use edit, not a create/edit Cartesian matrix; no all-character or other-driver credential-boundary claim is made.
checklist_items.1.5: Every public kind the server returns is selected in turn and the selection is asserted, not assumed from the click. After choosing an option the combobox is required to show exactly that kind's caption and nothing else, and reopening the popup is required to mark exactly one option as selected and that option is required to carry the same caption. The plan is not a sample: the observed directed pairs are compared against the full cross product of kinds and the case fails unless every ordered pair was exercised, so a kind added later that is never switched to breaks the run. The exact submitted value is checked separately on the real create - the POST body must equal the fixed object for the final kind - and the saved row is read back and compared field by field, including the requirement that credential roots belonging to other kinds are absent from the body, which is the runtime effect of the per-kind credential schema. On mutation evidence, only one probe counts: removing setKind from the select onChange fails the case while the credential fields of the newly chosen kind stop rendering. An attempt to pin the displayed value did not change the rendered selection, because antd keeps the chosen option in its own state, so that attempt is not offered as evidence for the caption assertion.
checklist_items.1.6: Every directed transition among the real public provider schemas is selected through the UI after filling old credential drafts. Schema-derived API-key, public/private-key, extra and endpoint controls have exact visibility, type, required flags and first defaults; absent controls unmount, old secrets/reset fields disappear and the name stays unchanged. Returning to pristine RunPod is followed by its actual exact create POST, which omits all hidden credential roots. This proves switching and final RunPod submission, not successful creation or persistence for every other driver.
checklist_items.1.7: Covered: a separate browser-created RunPod account fills only required name and API key, leaving the actual optional endpoint prefill https://api.runpod.io/v2 untouched. Exact POST201 body, independent detail GET, refreshed list/edit with empty secret, default-authority CONNECT/SNI/TLS and exact authenticated pods/key-registration calls agree; browser DELETE is followed by independent404 and empty list. The endpoint is present in wire JSON; this is not an omission claim.
checklist_items.1.8: covered: every RunPod create input used here reaches the exact POST body and the independent detail GET, and the optional endpoint's default is proven rather than assumed. The three controls are each asserted for type, placeholder, aria-required and the absence of a maxlength - none of these fields has a product maximum, so no bound is invented. A separate account is then created touching only the two required inputs and never the prefilled endpoint, and the POST body is compared exactly to {kind, name, api_key, endpoint: <the schema default>} followed by a detail read returning that same default, which is what an omitted optional field has to produce.
checklist_items.1.9: covered: While the create POST is held a second click and Enter send no further create, and the later 201 is the only stored provider
checklist_items.1.10: covered: The upstream 401 becomes HTTP 400 and the localized update-failed reason stays visible. The dialog and endpoint draft remain, the independent GET keeps endpoint A, and the later retry stores endpoint B
checklist_items.1.11: The name label has the no-colon class. On a freshly opened edit dialog, Escape closes it after the endpoint draft changes and sends no provider POST, PUT, or DELETE. The dialog is opened again, and the close button does the same. It is opened again, and Cancel does the same. After each of those dismissals the independent GET still has the saved name and endpoint.
checklist_items.1.12: On actual RunPod accounts, name-only and endpoint A-to-B edits preserve other configuration and authenticated key use. Empty/whitespace endpoint edits retain the old override according to merge semantics. A separately issued key B replaces A through the real UI; unchanged public GET configuration and actual UI Sync prove persisted B is used. Omitted, explicitly cleared and whitespace key edits retain B, including successful recovery after an invalid-header draft. This form has no account on/off or binding selector; no unsupported secret-clear or revoke/expiry/scope lifecycle is claimed.
checklist_items.1.13: Covered: two independent browser contexts open the same saved account. One writes another name; the original editor retains its stale draft and then writes last. Exact PUT bodies, independent GET after each write and the other session refresh prove the actual last-writer-wins contract. Deletion during an open editor remains outside this scenario.
checklist_items.1.14: Covered in this scenario: refreshed edit and independent GET match saved name/endpoint; real authenticated driver requests use the saved proxy and key.
checklist_items.1.15: The name label column has the left-label class and its text alignment is start. Tab from the type combobox reaches the name, then the API key, then the API endpoint. Add can be focused. Enter in the empty name sends no provider POST and the name stays empty. The upstream rejection shows the localized update-failed sentence. At 1440×900 the name, the API key, the API endpoint, Cancel, and Add are each inside the viewport, and the name does not overlap Add.
checklist_items.2.1: For the actual RunPod create/edit name, endpoint and API-key controls, accessible labels, localized hints/placeholders, input types, required flags and actual default/refilled values are checked. Held edit-detail loading disables incomplete fields and Save; after the real GET they are enabled, secrets stay blank, and the fixed RunPod kind has its own exact accessible label, disabled state and actual value. Untouched endpoint creation is checked through exact wire/GET and the default HTTPS boundary.
checklist_items.2.2: The actual RunPod name, endpoint and API key each exercise create/edit empty, pure whitespace, leading, trailing and both-sided spaces with exact browser JSON, independent GET/reopen and correction. Name create preserves raw spaces; edit trims nonblank names or retains the prior name. Endpoint create preserves raw empty/whitespace while using default HTTPS; blank edit retains the override and padded overrides persist raw. Create-empty key is frontend-refused; whitespace/leading/both-padded invalid credentials produce real401-to400 rejection without persistence, while trailing-only header whitespace follows real HTTP serialization. Blank/whitespace edits retain the stored key, proven by authenticated UI Sync; secrets are never returned by GET. No other-driver credential whitespace matrix is claimed.
checklist_items.2.3: Covered for the actual bounded display-name field: empty edit is refused inline without mutation; the owned account accepts one Unicode code point, 255 Chinese code points and 256 supplementary-Unicode code points, with exact PUT/GET/refreshed text and retained-key runtime validation. 257 code points receive exact FIELD_INVALID400 with the maximum256 reason, preserved draft, zero external calls and unchanged saved name. The original run-scoped name is restored. Counting is Unicode code points, not UTF-8 bytes or UTF-16 units; endpoint/API key have no invented string-length maximum.
checklist_items.2.4: Name is the only provider field with a character contract on the server - the create and update handlers validate it through one shared text validator, while the endpoint is only trimmed and has its trailing slashes removed and the credential fields are not character checked at all - so name is where the matrix belongs and it is exercised end to end. Chinese, English, digits and punctuation are typed, saved, and the saved row is read back; a raw CRLF string is pasted and required to arrive as a single line with all three parts intact before it is saved; a prohibited control character is pasted unchanged and the save is required to fail. Success is never inferred from the input: every stage asserts the exact PUT body, the exact status, the write count, and for the refusals the exact FIELD_INVALID body with its field and detail. The 256 code point limit is checked on both sides of the boundary and the oversized value must be refused. Proven by mutation: making the control-character test always return false turns the control stage into a 200 and the case fails on the expected status.
checklist_items.2.5: The server-side constraint this component has is not name uniqueness - provider names are not declared unique and the product permits two accounts with the same name - so the conflict is built against the constraint the API does enforce: concurrent writers on one record. Two real browser editors are opened on the same saved account. The second editor reads the record, renames it, and its PUT is asserted to succeed and to be what an independent reread returns. The first editor's still-open dialog is then asserted to keep its own draft rather than pick up the other writer's name, so the pre-conflict value survives on screen. Saving that draft is asserted to succeed as the last writer and to become what a reread returns, and the other session is reloaded and required to show only the final name with no row left under the intermediate one. Two writers, the stale draft retained, the last writer winning, and both sessions agreeing afterwards are all recorded as evidence. No mutation was performed for this item: the modal's draft lives in antd form state that a second session cannot reach, and the one probe that was tried - dropping the seeding guard so the effect re-seeds whenever it runs - left the case passing, because the effect does not re-run when another writer saves. The discriminating power here is therefore not demonstrated by a product mutation, and this reason does not imply one. What it does have is the second writer acting on the same record through a real browser and a real PUT, with both sessions' state confirmed by independent rereads.
checklist_items.2.6: Covered: actual clipboard permissions and Control+V paste the fixture name, custom endpoint and API key into all three real controls. Control+A/Backspace clear each; keyboard deletion/replacement restores exact values and sends zero management mutations. The secret is removed from clipboard. Multiline preservation is inapplicable to these single-line RunPod fields.
checklist_items.2.7: Covered in the available account-name surfaces: the scoped name includes literal 中文 & "quoted"; the saved list cell must have its exact original text and no b descendants, and refreshed edit input retains the same literal value. A product innerHTML mutant fails this family. This is literal escaping evidence, not a comprehensive XSS audit.

checklist_items.4.2: Actual UI saves reject FTP, hostless URL, nonnumeric and out-of-range ports and duplicated operation prefix with exact management errors. Malformed transport targets send no external request; the duplicated prefix reaches the strict fixture and gets404. Failed drafts and independent saved values remain unchanged, and corrected saves recover. Optional empty create uses the real default HTTPS endpoint, while empty edit retains its saved override.
checklist_items.4.3: For padded HTTP proxy URLs with actual port, path slashes and escaped query bytes, the real input value, exact browser JSON, independent stored GET and refreshed edit input preserve the raw endpoint. Driver-normalized outbound method/path/query is checked separately by the strict fixture; effective port/path/query cannot silently disappear. Empty endpoint storage remains distinct from runtime default fallback.
checklist_items.4.4: N/A: this form's endpoint is HTTP, not a node address, image reference or filesystem path.
checklist_items.4.5: Covered in this scenario: reopening and refreshing preserve each manually configured proxy endpoint.

checklist_items.7.1: Covered: schema/API key is required only on create; empty create is refused at the field without a mutation or page error, while pure whitespace reaches the real external401 and server400 without an account write. The draft remains. Password masking, real show/hide with unchanged value and zero mutations are checked before tracing secrets. Edit secret is optional, stays blank and omitted, and explicit whitespace retains the stored key as proved by actual authenticated validation calls.
checklist_items.7.2: Covered in this scenario: edit API key stays empty and omitted from the PUT body; authenticated upstream requests prove the stored value is retained.
checklist_items.7.3: N/A: the provider API key is supplied by the user, not an application-issued one-time credential.
checklist_items.7.4: Covered: a fresh key is used for a real action, not merely stored. Key A creates the account and the external fixture sees the registration with A; the secret is then rotated to B and only B authenticates afterwards, so an update that ignored the new key could not pass. An error is exercised on the same credential: a key carrying a NUL is refused before any external request with the real transport reason, the draft is cleared, and the stored B still authenticates; empty and whitespace-only edits keep B and change no other field. The remaining clauses do not apply to this credential - it is the vendor's API key, which the platform cannot revoke, is not scoped per caller, and carries no expiry the platform tracks, so those are recorded under 7.3 and 7.5 rather than claimed here.
checklist_items.7.5: N/A: this case uses vendor credentials, not platform or inference token controls.
checklist_items.7.6: Ordinary raw provider list/detail GETs, a real secret-bearing upstream SSH400 error reaching the best-effort WARN/logstore boundary and a secret-bearing pod403 error reaching Sync HTTP424 are scanned before artifact redaction. Exact safe operation/status errors and actual raw HTTP/WARN log records are required; empty logs cannot pass. Secret entry and hostile responses occur with tracing stopped; tracing resumes only after raw response/log checks. Final raw logs, DOM/clipboard and artifacts are checked. Provider-account credential download/export is absent by UI/API source audit, not treated as an unexecuted successful download.
checklist_items.7.7: N/A: no management password change or platform-token revocation is performed.
checklist_items.11.4: covered: the public and private provider tables are two ResourceTables with two ids, driven in one session. A movable column is hidden on /providers, the private page is then opened and is required to still show that column - so the choice did not follow the user - and choosing on the private table is required to add a second stored layout, so the two ids are shown to hold separate entries rather than sharing one. Returning to the public page is required to bring back exactly the layout it had, not the private one. Clearing the stored layouts restores the defaults, which is what makes the earlier readings about the stored copy and not about page state. Proven by mutation: giving both scopes one table id makes the hidden column follow the user to the other page and the case fails.
checklist_items.11.1: covered: on the real public provider list, whose saved layout key carries the providers-public table id, the Type column's resize separator is driven with the keyboard and two ArrowRight presses are required to widen exactly that column by two 16px steps (160 -> 192) while every other column's own width is required to be unchanged, and the committed width is required to be the value written into the stored layout. Forty ArrowLeft presses are then required to stop at 64, two further presses are required to change nothing, and the stored widths are required to hold that same 64, so the minimum is a positive product value rather than a floor of zero. Content layout at that minimum is read from the real row this case created: each of the seven cells is required to keep a positive box, adjacent cells are required not to overlap, and the row is required to still carry text. A reload is required to rebuild the table out of the stored copy and bring back 64, so the value is a local preference and not page state. Nothing is asserted against the database: the layout is read from localStorage under the table's own id. Proven by mutation on the provider table: removing the minimum clamp from ResizableHeaderCell so the width is only rounded lets the column reach -448, and the case fails on the positive-minimum assertion ("the column did not stop at a positive minimum below its start width: -448"). The same clamp was also killed on api-keys; this is a second, independent kill recorded from this table rather than a claim borrowed from there.
checklist_items.11.2: covered: the settings drawer's Status checkbox is required to start checked, hiding it is required to uncheck it, and the rendered header row is required to lose exactly that one column while keeping every other column in its place. The stored layout is required to record exactly that one hidden key. A reload is required to keep the column absent, so the choice survives out of storage. Checking it again is required to restore the full column set. A keyboard drag on the Type handle (Space, ArrowDown, Space) is required to write an order in which the type key directly follows the instances key, and the rendered header row is required to show that same new slot, which is then required to survive a reload. The drawer's reset button is required to restore the default header row and to clear the stored widths, and that result is required again after a reload. Every layout change is required to issue zero provider writes. The drawer's hide handler is the same product code as the one killed on api-keys. A no-op setHidden built for this case is killed before this item is reached, by the earlier two-table isolation step of the same run ("the public table kept the column that was hidden: Type"), so this item's own hide step is not offered as a separate kill; the provider table is where the 6-column order and the real row are observed.
checklist_items.11.3: covered: the name and actions columns are required to appear in the drawer as checked and disabled checkboxes, and the name column is required to offer no drag handle and no hide control, so neither can be hidden or moved. The older-build clause is driven through the stored layout itself: a saved copy written into localStorage naming a column this build does not declare is required not to render that column, not to lose or invent a column, to still apply the surviving saved order (the saved first movable column is required to be rendered first among the movable columns, after the leading name column), to still apply the saved width of a known column sitting next to the unknown one, and to raise no page error. A stored copy that is not readable at all is required to fall back to the exact default header row with no page error. The locked-checkbox clause is the same disabled attribute already killed on api-keys, re-verified here. The unknown-column fallback is an equivalent mutation: dropping the known.has filter from parseColumnPrefs does not change what is rendered, because arrangeColumns re-resolves each saved key through the column map and drops the ones that resolve to nothing, so a mutant built from that change passes this case and is honestly recorded as not mutation-proven. The unreadable-layout fallback is likewise not mutation-proven.
